Distributionally robust optimal scheduling of urban multi-energy wastewater treatment plants under multiple uncertainties
Greenhouse gas and economic assessments of biochar-based composite panels from forest residues
abstract: Among other threats to forests across the western U.S., large-scale outbreaks of mountain pine beetle have generated extensive volumes of low-value forest residues that increase wildfire risk while remaining underutilized as a carbon resource. Converting these residues into high-value biochar products offers a pathway for carbon stabilization and value creation, yet most existing markets for biochar remain relatively low value. This study represents the first system-level assessment of biochar-based composite panels that jointly evaluates life-cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and techno-economic performance for biochar-based panel products at industrial scale. The modeled system integrates distributed biochar production using portable pyrolysis units with centralized panel manufacturing that uses kraft lignin as a renewable binder. In addition to a base-case (BC) configuration representing conventional biochar-lignin composite panel production, five alternative scenarios are modeled in which panels undergo secondary pyrolysis treatments at different temperatures and processing conditions associated with potential adsorption, structural, or fire-resistant applications. Cradle-to-gate GHG emissions range from 311 to 565 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 . In addition, an illustrative 100-year carbon retention scenario based on assumed long-term biochar stability results in net GHG balances ranging from −343 to −750 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 . Minimum selling price values range from 548 to 1101 US$/m 3 depending on panel type and processing conditions. The BC panel configuration falls toward the higher end of conventional particleboard and MDF price benchmarks, while the estimated MSPs of pyrolyzed panel configurations fall within or below the price ranges of selected benchmark materials used in water remediation and fire-resistant composite applications. These comparisons provide market-price context for the modeled MSPs but do not establish functional equivalence or commercial competitiveness, which require experimental validation.

title: Morphology-aware bidirectional state-space model for power prediction in CNC milling
Economic and environmental assessment of waste-derived aviation fuels using agent-based modeling under carbon pricing
abstract: Limited attention has been given to how environmental performance and economic incentives jointly shape aviation fuel adoption under evolving policy conditions. Most existing Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) studies rely on aggregated optimization models that assume equilibrium conditions, overlooking decentralized decision-making and actor heterogeneity. This study addresses this gap by framing the adoption of SAF as a complex adaptive system, where diverse flight agents respond to economic and regulatory incentives, producing fleet-level outcomes through decentralized operational decisions. An integrated framework is developed, combining life cycle assessment (LCA), techno-economic data, and agent-based modeling (ABM), simulating fuel selection at the individual flight level. By integrating environmental assessment with economic optimization, the model allows analysis at both flight and fleet levels. Results show that a 50% pyrolysis bio-oil blend consistently minimizes total operational cost under carbon pricing, reducing fleet-level costs from USD 9.38 billion for operating on 100% conventional jet fuel baseline to USD 4.7 billion while achieving significant lifecycle emissions reductions. The framework enables testing of alternative policy instruments, such as carbon pricing and blending mandates, providing practical insight into the aviation decarbonization pathway. Future research will incorporate endogenous supply–demand interactions, dynamic fuel pricing, infrastructure and resource constraints, and stochastic decision-making to better capture evolving SAF markets and improve the framework's applicability.

title: Bi-objective pareto low-carbon automatic demand response of energy-intensive enterprises accommodating users’ electricity consumption habits and behaviors
Organic copper substitution mitigates feed-derived copper emissions by enhancing bioefficacy and redox–microbiota homeostasis in Eriocheir sinensis

Chemical upcycling method for complete binder replacement from recycled asphalt shingle (RAS) binder using renewable chemistry
Power production and emergy-based sustainability in port areas
abstract: Port activities represent an outstanding sector in Blue Economy, with a contribution of approximately 11% to the Gross Value Added of the Blue Economy in the European Union. In addition, Blue Economy guidelines for Trans-European Transport Network — TEN-T — consider the deployment of structures and facilities enforcing clean On-Shore Power Supply — OPS — for ships at berth, and sustainable marine transport and port activities. This paper presents a comprehensive emergy-based sustainability assessment on the improvement of port areas with power supply systems based on Oscillating Water Column technology — OWC — to be used as specific OPS facilities, grid supply or ultimate storage systems. Emergy evaluation accounts for materials, machinery and workers, as well as their direct and indirect CO 2 emissions and embodied energy — eMergy —. Emergy-based indexes are calculated to appropriately quantify the degree of sustainability and renewability of a marine project, its dependence on social investments and the pressure on local ecosystems. A case study of OWC power facility commissioning in a port terminal project is presented for a better focusing. Without loss of generality, results show that the implementation of OWC power facility into the port system improves the overall sustainability, renewability, emergy-based indicators, as well as a reduction in CO 2 emissions, even if breakwater construction and port activities are not sustainable solely, involving non-renewable resources and fluxes from the environment and society. Moreover, the emergy budget allows to analyse the evolution of sustainability during the operational phase due to delays in construction and operational stops, showing that emergy accounting is a valuable tool for long-term management and planning of port infrastructure regarding sustainability.

title: Synergistic evaluation of pollutants and carbon emissions in typical spent lithium-ion batteries recycling processes
Uncovering the heterogeneous effects of China's Organic-Substitute-Chemical-Fertilizer policy: The role of local conditions in shaping distinct policy responses
Mechanical harvesting of cyanobacterial blooms shifts greenhouse gas potential to post-harvest sludge in a hypereutrophic lake
Experimental investigation of phosphorus and potassium recovery from chicken manure incineration ash (CMIA) using a mixed nitric acid–oxalic acid system
Basin-scale coupling between water-resource protection priority areas and urban–agricultural–ecological configuration typologies: Evidence from the Dongting Lake Basin, China
abstract: Climate change, urbanization, and intensified resource development are increasing pressure on freshwater systems and creating a need for spatially differentiated basin-scale protection. This study develops an integrated evaluation-configuration-diagnosis framework for the Dongting Lake Basin (DLB) from 2000 to 2023. A Water Resource Protection Importance Index (WRPI) and multiscale sensitivity analysis were used to identify stable high-demand areas. Class-level aggregation indices (CLUMPY) characterized the aggregation of urban, agricultural, and ecological spaces and identified stable spatial configurations. Spatial overlay delineated coupled priority areas, while an obstacle-degree model diagnosed municipal-level constraint structures. Stable high-demand areas were concentrated in the southern and southwestern basin, and their core distribution remained consistent across grid scales. In the urban-agricultural-ecological sequence, Low-Low-Low (LLL) and Low-High-High (LHH) were the dominant stable configurations, accounting for 40.99% and 31.62% of the total stable-configuration area, respectively. Overall, 90.96% of stable high-demand areas overlapped with stable configuration units, with LLL and LHH jointly accounting for 71.08% of the total overlap. The WRPI obstacle structure remained stable over time and was dominated by constraints related to Water Resource Conditions and Water Resource Development Potential, although their relative importance varied among municipalities and configuration contexts. Integrating municipal obstacle structures with stable configurations connected basin-scale priority assessment with specific spatial implementation contexts. The framework supports spatially targeted and differentiated water-resource governance in the DLB and provides a transferable workflow for other large basins.

A DPP-enabled decision support system for end-of-life strategy recommendation
abstract: The transition towards a circular economy requires reliable lifecycle information to support end-of-life (EoL) decision-making. Using a sample luminaire, this study proposes a decision-support component designed to enhance Digital Product Passport (DPP) functionality by integrating lifecycle data, condition monitoring, predictive analytics, and stakeholder priorities for end-of-life strategy selection. Guided by Axiomatic Design principles, a prototype platform was developed and demonstrated for the representative lighting fixture. The system combines product information, sensor-derived condition indicators, remaining useful life estimation, anomaly detection, and multi-criteria user preferences to generate probabilistic recommendations for alternative EoL strategies. An interactive dashboard was implemented to provide an intuitive user interface and support transparency and usability. Industrial evaluation with domain experts confirmed the conceptual validity and practical relevance of the approach while highlighting challenges related to data governance, interoperability, cybersecurity, and business model integration. The findings demonstrate the potential of intelligent DPP-enabled systems to support circular decision-making and sustainable lifecycle management.

title: The policy triad: Designing the interactions of incentive, constraint, and enabling instruments on ecosystem value realization
Novel and efficient removal of impurities from spent silicon contact mass via an in situ copper-catalyzed leaching process
The politics of forest biomass co-firing in Indonesia: Explaining policy implementation through the Actor–Network–Interest (ANI) framework
Multidimensional contributions to the water-energy-food nexus: Interpretable evidence from cities in China's Yellow river region
Voyage-based optimisation of biofuel bunkering strategies using real ship data
abstract: Maritime decarbonisation requires operationally realistic strategies that account for fuel availability and evolving regulatory constraints. This study presents a data-driven framework for optimising biofuel bunkering strategies for a real-world bulk carrier by integrating historical voyage data, port-specific biofuel availability, lifecycle emissions, and regulatory performance metrics. Historical voyage data are used to reconstruct routes and estimate energy demand. Candidate biofuels derived from different feedstocks, including FAME, HVO, and biodiesel blends (B24 and B30), are evaluated using a multi-objective optimisation model (NSGA-III) considering: (i) the overall WTW GHG emission intensity, (ii) lost cargo volume, and (iii) annual FuelEU compliance margin. Results show that fuel type primarily governs WTW emissions, while feedstock availability influences high-biofuel-share pathways, and port-level biofuel availability dominates optimal bunkering strategies. Waste-based biofuels achieve the lowest WTW emission intensities (≤16 gCO 2 eq/MJ), outperforming animal fat-derived (20-22 gCO 2 eq/MJ), crop-based biofuels (44-51 gCO 2 eq/MJ), and biodiesel blends (>70 gCO 2 eq/MJ). Cargo volume loss remains minimal (<1%) across all scenarios. Regulatory analysis indicates that crop-based biofuels become non-compliant with FuelEU GHG intensity targets by 2045. The proposed framework enables actionable, voyage-specific decarbonisation strategies and highlights the critical role of fuel type, feedstock selection, port-level fuel availability and biofuel supply development.

title: City-scale dynamic mining zoning for source-based damage reduction and efficient coal resource utilization in high-groundwater-table coal–farmland overlapped areas
Tax coal or subsidize clean capacity? A differential game of incumbent utilities’ energy transition
Spatial distribution and influencing factors of data center water usage effectiveness in China
Global coal mining carbon emissions: Spatiotemporal evolution patterns, driving mechanisms and China's decoupling path under carbon neutrality
Decarbonizing Canadian commercial aviation: Efficiency gains, sustainable aviation fuel, and structural limits to emissions reduction
abstract: Commercial aviation is a difficult-to-abate sector in which traffic growth can offset improvements in operational and fuel efficiency. This study evaluates the decarbonization trajectory of Canadian commercial aviation from 2015 to 2025, examining whether efficiency gains have been sufficient to counteract activity-driven emissions growth and represent a persistent structural improvement. This study analyzes eight open-government analytical datasets, supplemented by two external benchmark sources. Kaya–Logarithmic Mean Divisia Index (LMDI) decomposition quantifies the contributions of activity, stage length, load factor, and fuel intensity to CO 2 emissions, while trend and structural-break analyses assess changes in emissions intensity. Complementary analyses examine airport recovery, an exploratory association between occurrence-based turbofan representation and aviation incidents, and sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) scenarios. Annual CO 2 intensity declined significantly over the non-pandemic period, and fuel-intensity improvements avoided approximately 2.9 Mt CO 2 between 2015 and 2019. However, activity growth added approximately 5.3 Mt CO 2 , outweighing these gains. Monthly analysis identifies a major structural disruption at the onset of COVID-19 followed by a subsequent recovery regime. Airport recovery was heterogeneous, while the safety analysis identified an exploratory negative association between occurrence-based turbofan share and incident counts. Under the SAF uptake and traffic-growth scenarios evaluated, fuel substitution alone does not fully offset projected activity-driven emissions growth through 2030. Overall, efficiency improvements have reduced Canadian aviation carbon intensity but remain insufficient to achieve sustained reductions in absolute emissions under continued traffic growth, highlighting the need to evaluate accelerated SAF deployment alongside additional mitigation measures. When the observed fuel-efficiency trend and the 5% SAF blend are evaluated jointly, however, projected 2030 emissions fall to approximately 19.8 Mt—below the 2025 level of about 20.1 Mt—so that the two levers together offset essentially the entire traffic-driven increment.

title: Incremental learning-based dynamic multiobjective optimization algorithm for disassembly line balancing
Identification of descriptors for thiophene desulfurization and heavy metal immobilization over K-modified calcium-based materials
Mass and functionality based exergy analysis of different rapeseed protein production routes
abstract: Rapeseed proteins are among the outstanding plant-based proteins due to their favorable interfacial functionality. This study evaluates the resource use of the most common rapeseed protein production routes – acidic precipitation, ultrafiltration and wet mild fractionation – using an exergy-based approach. The exergy consumption is normalized based on both product mass and protein functionality. Mass-based assessment indicates that the routes producing dry rapeseed protein concentrate exhibit relatively low exergy efficiencies (12.3 – 20.7%), mainly due to production of a single useful stream and dilute processing conditions that intensify the drying-related exergy demand. Wet mild fractionation shows the highest exergy efficiency at 47.3%, by distributing resource inputs across two useful products, oleosome cream and proteins. When evaluated based on protein functionality, however, ultrafiltration-based recovery of proteins from rapeseed meal and acid precipitation from cold-pressed cake emerge as the least exergy-intensive options to produce rapeseed protein-based emulsifiers. Therefore, the study shows that the resource use efficiency of a process is strongly dependent on the chosen evaluation criterion and highlights the importance of functionality-oriented valorisation of useful streams to enhance the efficiency of resources use.

title: Automated detection of morphologically diverse microplastics using ensemble deep learning
Reaction and microstructural insights into UHPC with carbonated steel slag at different substitution ratios
abstract: Basic oxygen furnace (BOF) slag, a major type of steel slag generated during steelmaking, offers significant potential as a low-carbon cement replacement. Carbonation pretreatment has been developed to enhance both the filler effect and the pozzolanic reactivity of steel slag powder (SSP), enabling partial replacement of cement with carbonated SSP (CSSP) in ultra-high-performance concrete (UHPC). However, the reaction mechanisms governing CSSP in UHPC remain insufficiently understood. In this study, the phase assemblage, calcium-silicate-hydrate (C-S-H) characteristics, and microstructure of UHPC substituted with CSSP were investigated. The results revealed that the optimal mechanical performance was achieved at a 30 % replacement level, with the compressive strength being 10.0 % higher than that of the untreated SSP mixture. At moderate CSSP contents, carbonation-derived calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) acted synergistically as both a micro filler and nucleation site. Consequently, UHPC substituted with CSSP exhibited a higher degree of hydration (DoH), an increased mean chain length (MCL) of C-S-H, and higher pore fractal dimensions than UHPC with untreated SSP. However, at 40-50 % CSSP substitution levels, cement clinker dilution becomes dominant and outweighs the compensatory physical filler effect and chemical contribution of CaCO 3 . Although additional carbonate ions can promote the formation of AFm-type carbonate phases, the reduced availability of reactive clinker limits CH generation and decreases the Ca/Si ratio of the C-S-H gel. Consequently, C-S-H formation becomes insufficient, leading to limited pore refinement, increased pore irregularity, and a less dense UHPC matrix.

title: Is Metro-based logistics always greener? A carbon emission break-even analysis under the trend of electrification and multi-dimensional spatiotemporal constraints
Thermally treated oyster shells elevate biofilm viability and nutrient removal in sediment microbial fuel cells
Systematic power decarbonization strategies for sustainable steel manufacturing: an integrated modeling framework combining process regulation and technology integration
From data-driven analysis to system development: A framework for developing an ease-of-disassembly evaluation system based on experimental data and multi-source text
Feasibility study of stabilizing soft soil in the Jianghan Plain using one-part alkali-activated materials developed by iron and steel slags
When does Remanufacturing versus new product manufacture pay off? Derivation of a commercial ReMan formula and decision logic based on empirical ratio analyses across multi company production data
abstract: Remanufacturing (ReMan) is an ecologically and economically promising production approach and business model for enabling a circular economy and conserving resources. However, its adoption across industrial sectors remains limited due to a lack of knowledge and guidance on the product characteristics and cost factors that support a profitable ReMan business. Therefore, this study derives a commercial ReMan formula linking those production cost metrics that significantly influence profitability with corresponding product characteristics. The formula is based on a ratio analysis of product characteristics and commercial data from successful ReMan cases (n=355) covering various product categories from two mechanical engineering companies. Our results show that the economic efficiency of ReMan business is primarily driven by increasing net and material costs, increasing weight, and greater product complexity including part count. In contrast, assembly costs, testing costs, logistics costs, overhead surcharges, and the expected CO2e-surcharge savings of ReMan products exert only a marginal impact on cost-effectiveness. Based on the findings, a ReMan formula and decision logic are developed, incorporating four identified key commercial metrics: (1) the value of reusable ReMan components, (2) repurchase price of the used product, (3) costs of disassembly, cleaning, and inspection of the used product, and (4) the price delta between new and remanufactured product. Future research could extend the derived ReMan formula by investigating absolute cost thresholds for critical ReMan activities, such as disassembly, cleaning, and inspection, to identify economic barriers limiting ReMan adoption, particularly in consumer goods markets and further industrial sectors.

title: Dual regulation of CO2 hydrate formation by clay mineral and kinetic promoter: mechanistic insights for marine sequestration
When is carbonation-cured concrete actually cleaner? A systematic review, a net-benefit condition framework, and a proposed minimum reporting set for CO2 mineralization in cement-based products
abstract: Cement manufacture releases 7–8% of global anthropogenic CO 2 , most of it from the irreducible calcination of limestone. Accelerated carbonation curing mineralizes captured CO 2 inside cement-based products. Whether it delivers a net climate benefit, and under what conditions, cannot presently be answered from the published life-cycle assessment (LCA) literature. A reproducible PRISMA 2020 search (713 records), confirmed against Web of Science, identified seventeen studies declaring a functional unit, a cradle-to-gate boundary and a non-carbonated comparator. Their outcomes cannot be pooled: five functional-unit bases, seventeen comparators, baselines spanning 280–540 kg CO 2 -eq/m 3 , and results reported in structurally different forms. That incommensurability is the first finding. In most of the set the benefit tracks avoided Portland clinker rather than mineralized CO 2 : every reduction above 10% involves clinker being substituted or eliminated, and one study reports 5–8 kg CO 2 -eq per tonne of cement for each 1% of clinker replaced. Across matched comparisons the isolated effect of carbonation spans both signs — from a 3.1–11.3% net increase once process electricity is charged to reductions of 37%. Varying only the CO 2 recovery route for one product returns 68%, 77% and 71%. Of twenty-five papers reporting an environmental result, eight omit a functional unit or system boundary. A net-benefit condition model accounts for the spread, and a five-field minimum reporting set mapped to EN 15804, ISO 21930 and ISO 14025 is proposed so future LCAs can be synthesized.

title: Does memory of hydrological processes and atmospheric dryness influence forest fire intensity: A case study in the western Himalayas
When circularity gains diverge from social-equity outcomes: A justice-oriented agent-based scenario-comparison model with an Amsterdam case study
abstract: This study develops a justice-oriented agent-based model (ABM) to examine how everyday circular-economy (CE) practices, spatial access to CE infrastructure and labor-market assumptions jointly shape distributive urban outcomes. Using Amsterdam as an illustrative case, the model represents household sorting, bulky-item drop-off and repair behavior under uneven access to sorting containers, recycling centers, repair cafés and waste-burden locations. Four CE policy scenarios are compared through replicated simulations, plausibility checks and extended sensitivity screening. The results show that CE-active scenarios generate circular activity relative to the Linear reference, while mean local CE activation and flow-based citywide CE throughput do not always follow the same pattern. Under the model's assumed negative reduced-form CE–unemployment coupling, CE-active scenarios also produce lower simulated unemployment. This conditional result reflects the specified labor-market mechanism and does not imply that CE policies generally cause unemployment to fall. Spatial-advantage inequality is higher in CE-active scenarios when scenario-specific opportunity activation interacts with uneven access and burden layers, while accumulated-resource inequality does not automatically decline under stronger CE support. The main contribution is a transparent scenario-analysis testbed that connects household heterogeneity, spatial opportunity, behavioral mechanisms and distributional consequences, helping to explore when aggregate circularity gains may diverge from justice-oriented urban outcomes.

title: Cleaner peri-urban agricultural transitions under nitrogen-related water constraints: A teacher-validated evaluation of land-use alternatives in Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands
abstract: Peri-urban agriculture is increasingly expected to contribute to sustainable urban development while reducing the environmental pressures associated with land-use change and water-quality degradation. A key challenge is how to compare alternative agricultural configurations that maintain productive land use while lowering nitrogen-related environmental burdens before implementation. This study develops a teacher-validated framework for evaluating cleaner peri-urban agricultural land-use alternatives, using Almere Oosterwold, the Netherlands, as a living-lab case. We combine the InVEST Nutrient Delivery Ratio (NDR) model as a process-based teacher model with deep surrogate models and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to generate and screen alternative crop-pattern configurations under explicit feasibility constraints. Candidate Pareto solutions are then materialised and re-evaluated with the teacher model, which separates rapid screening from final environmental interpretation. The framework is designed around an explicit scale mismatch: land-use decisions are taken on individual parcels and governance blocks, whereas nitrogen impacts accumulate over the whole planning domain. Under the available data regime, the governance-aligned graph surrogate outperforms pixel-level emulation and provides acceptable screening fidelity on the 32 × 32 intervention grid. Teacher validation shows that the best alternatives lower domain-integrated subsurface nitrogen export by up to 998.55 kg N yr −1 (ΔN = −998.55 kg N yr −1 ), equivalent to about 10.8% of the baseline, at an intervention footprint of about 2392 ha. Screening reliability is further quantified through rank association, top- K precision and Pareto overlap. The contribution of the study is to link cleaner peri-urban agricultural transition, nitrogen-related environmental management and land-use alternative appraisal in a single reproducible framework for comparing productive configurations under water-quality constraints. More broadly, the study shows how rapid alternative exploration and teacher-validated environmental evidence can be combined to support cleaner and more sustainable peri-urban land-use transitions.

title: Dynamic responses of Rhodobacter capsulatus to light and oxygen cultivated on H2 and CO2: Effects on the productivity of biomass, protein, pigments, coenzyme Q10, and antioxidant capacity
Spatiotemporal variability of pavement material costs: Implications for maintenance strategies and economic-environmental sustainability
Two-stage robust optimization of shared energy storage system in multi-community energy systems considering electric vehicle flexibility
Predicting staggered carbon peaking in the logistics industry: Evidence from China's new international land-sea trade corridor
Advancing NO2 exposure assessment with hourly seamless retrievals from geostationary satellites

Cadmium bioavailability during flooding–drainage in paddy soils: Spatiotemporal associations with dissolved organic matter transformation and iron speciation
